## HX-CP-001

**API server allows anonymous requests** — medium, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver configurations that do not set --anonymous-auth=false and do not use a structured authentication configuration.

**Why it matters:** Anonymous requests are attributed to system:anonymous. Any RBAC binding to that user or system:unauthenticated, made in error or by an attacker, becomes reachable by anyone who can reach the API server.

**Remediation:** Set --anonymous-auth=false. If anonymous health checks are required, use a structured --authentication-config that limits anonymous access to the health endpoints.

**Known limitations:** When --authentication-config is set, its contents are not yet inspected.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.1 Ensure that the --anonymous-auth argument is set to false](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Authentication](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-002

**API server authorization disabled or weak** — critical, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver configurations whose --authorization-mode is unset (defaulting to AlwaysAllow) or includes AlwaysAllow, and those that do not enable RBAC (medium).

**Why it matters:** With AlwaysAllow, every authenticated request is permitted: any service account token is effectively cluster-admin.

**Remediation:** Set --authorization-mode=Node,RBAC.

**Known limitations:** When --authorization-config is set, its contents are not yet inspected.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.6 Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.8 Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument includes RBAC](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-003

**API server audit logging not configured** — medium, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver configurations without an audit policy, or with a policy but no log or webhook backend.

**Why it matters:** Without audit logs there is no record of who did what through the API. Incidents cannot be investigated and malicious activity cannot be detected.

**Remediation:** Set --audit-policy-file to a reviewed policy and --audit-log-path (with --audit-log-maxage, -maxbackup, -maxsize) or --audit-webhook-config-file.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.16 Ensure that the --audit-log-path argument is set](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 3.2.1 Ensure that a minimal audit policy is created](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Audit Logging and Threat Detection › Logging › Kubernetes native audit logging configuration](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-004

**Control-plane profiling enabled** — low, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler without --profiling=false.

**Why it matters:** Profiling endpoints reveal detailed program and system information and add an unnecessary attack surface.

**Remediation:** Set --profiling=false on each control-plane component.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.15 Ensure that the --profiling argument is set to false](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.3.2 Ensure that the --profiling argument is set to false](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.4.1 Ensure that the --profiling argument is set to false](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Control plane hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-005

**Weak admission control** — high, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver configurations that enable AlwaysAdmit (high), disable PodSecurity (high), or do not enable NodeRestriction (medium).

**Why it matters:** Admission control is where cluster-wide guardrails are enforced. AlwaysAdmit bypasses it; without PodSecurity, nothing blocks privileged pods; without NodeRestriction, a compromised kubelet can modify any node or pod object.

**Remediation:** Remove AlwaysAdmit, keep PodSecurity enabled, and add NodeRestriction to --enable-admission-plugins.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.10 Ensure that the admission control plugin AlwaysAdmit is not set](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.14 Ensure that the admission control plugin NodeRestriction is set](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Control plane hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-006

**etcd not protected by mutual TLS** — high, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects etcd without client and peer certificate authentication (or using self-signed auto-TLS), and kube-apiserver without etcd client certificates.

**Why it matters:** etcd stores every object in the cluster, including all Secrets. Anyone who can talk to etcd without a client certificate can read or rewrite the entire cluster state, bypassing authentication, authorization and audit.

**Remediation:** Run etcd with --client-cert-auth=true, --peer-client-cert-auth=true, CA-issued certificates (not --auto-tls), and give kube-apiserver --etcd-cafile, --etcd-certfile and --etcd-keyfile.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 2.1 Ensure that the --cert-file and --key-file arguments are set as appropriate](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 2.2 Ensure that the --client-cert-auth argument is set to true](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 2.3 Ensure that the --auto-tls argument is not set to true](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 2.5 Ensure that the --peer-client-cert-auth argument is set to true](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 2.6 Ensure that the --peer-auto-tls argument is not set to true](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.23 Ensure that the --etcd-certfile and --etcd-keyfile arguments are set as appropriate](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.26 Ensure that the --etcd-cafile argument is set as appropriate](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Control plane hardening › Etcd](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-007

**Secrets not encrypted at rest** — medium, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver configurations without --encryption-provider-config.

**Why it matters:** Without encryption at rest, Secrets are stored in etcd in plain form; an etcd backup or disk snapshot discloses every credential in the cluster.

**Remediation:** Configure --encryption-provider-config with a KMS v2 provider (preferred) or aescbc/secretbox, covering at least secrets, and rewrite existing secrets.

**Known limitations:** The contents of the encryption configuration (e.g. an identity provider listed first) are not yet inspected.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.27 Ensure that the --encryption-provider-config argument is set as appropriate](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Encryption](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-008

**API server does not verify kubelet certificates** — medium, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects kube-apiserver configurations without --kubelet-certificate-authority.

**Why it matters:** Without it the API server does not verify kubelet serving certificates, so exec, logs and port-forward traffic can be intercepted by anyone able to impersonate a node on the network.

**Remediation:** Enable kubelet serving certificate bootstrap (serverTLSBootstrap) and set --kubelet-certificate-authority to the CA that signs them.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.5 Ensure that the --kubelet-certificate-authority argument is set as appropriate](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Control plane hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-CP-009

**Admission webhook fails open** — medium, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects ValidatingWebhookConfigurations and MutatingWebhookConfigurations whose webhooks guard workload, RBAC or networking resources with failurePolicy: Ignore.

**Why it matters:** A policy webhook that fails open is bypassed whenever it is unavailable. An attacker who can slow down, crash or partition the webhook service can then create workloads the policy would have rejected.

**Remediation:** Set failurePolicy: Fail for security policy webhooks, run them highly available, and exclude only the namespaces needed to recover the webhook itself.

**Known limitations:** Webhooks that are not security controls (e.g. defaulting or metrics) are reported too when they fail open; waive them with a justification.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Control plane hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Dynamic admission control: failure policy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#failure-policy)

## HX-CP-010

**Admission webhook served from outside the cluster** — medium, control-plane

**Checks:** Detects admission webhooks that guard workload, RBAC or networking resources and are called by URL (clientConfig.url) rather than through an in-cluster Service. Mutating webhooks are reported as high: they can rewrite every pod they see.

**Why it matters:** The API server sends every matching object to the webhook and trusts its answer. A webhook reached by URL puts that trust in whatever answers at that DNS name and in the network between — outside the cluster's RBAC, NetworkPolicy and audit. A compromised or spoofed mutating webhook can inject privileged containers into every pod in the cluster.

**Remediation:** Serve the webhook from a Service in the cluster (clientConfig.service). If an external endpoint is unavoidable, pin its CA with caBundle, scope rules and namespaceSelector narrowly, and monitor the endpoint as part of the control plane.

**Known limitations:** URLs that resolve to the control-plane host (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) are treated as local. Whether the endpoint is actually trustworthy cannot be judged from the manifest.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Control plane hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Threat model](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Dynamic admission control: contacting the webhook](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#contact-the-webhook)

## HX-NET-001

**Namespace without default-deny ingress** — medium, networking

**Checks:** Detects namespaces containing workloads where no NetworkPolicy selects all pods and denies ingress by default.

**Why it matters:** Kubernetes allows all pod-to-pod traffic by default. Without a default-deny policy, one compromised pod can reach every service in the cluster, including databases and internal admin endpoints.

**Remediation:** Add a NetworkPolicy with podSelector: {} and policyTypes: [Ingress], then add policies allowing only required traffic. Confirm your CNI plugin enforces NetworkPolicy.

**Known limitations:** Only NetworkPolicies present in the scanned input are considered. CNI-specific policies (e.g. CiliumNetworkPolicy, Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy) are not yet understood.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.3.2 Ensure that all Namespaces have NetworkPolicies defined](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Network policies](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-NET-002

**Namespace without default-deny egress** — low, networking

**Checks:** Detects namespaces containing workloads where no NetworkPolicy selects all pods and denies egress by default.

**Why it matters:** Unrestricted egress lets a compromised pod reach cloud metadata services, the API server, other tenants and the internet for command-and-control or exfiltration.

**Remediation:** Add a NetworkPolicy with podSelector: {} and policyTypes: [Egress], then allow DNS and the specific destinations each workload needs.

**Known limitations:** As for HX-NET-001.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.3.2 Ensure that all Namespaces have NetworkPolicies defined](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Network policies](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-NET-003

**Service exposed outside the cluster** — medium, networking

**Checks:** Detects LoadBalancer Services without loadBalancerSourceRanges (medium) and NodePort Services (low).

**Why it matters:** LoadBalancer and NodePort services are reachable from outside the cluster network. Without source restrictions, internal tools exposed this way are reachable by anyone who can route to the load balancer or nodes.

**Remediation:** Use ClusterIP behind an Ingress with authentication where possible; otherwise set loadBalancerSourceRanges to the networks that need access.

**Known limitations:** Cloud-provider annotations that make a load balancer internal are not yet recognised.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-NET-004

**Service with externalIPs** — medium, networking

**Checks:** Detects Services that set spec.externalIPs.

**Why it matters:** externalIPs let a Service claim traffic for arbitrary IP addresses, enabling in-cluster traffic interception (CVE-2020-8554). Few legitimate setups need it.

**Remediation:** Remove externalIPs, and block the field cluster-wide with an admission policy (e.g. the DenyServiceExternalIPs admission plugin).

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 1.2.3 Ensure that the --DenyServiceExternalIPs is set](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [CVE-2020-8554](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97076)

## HX-NET-005

**Ingress without TLS** — medium, networking

**Checks:** Detects Ingresses with no TLS configuration, and Ingress hosts not covered by any TLS entry.

**Why it matters:** Traffic to hosts without TLS crosses the network in clear text: credentials, session cookies and API tokens can be read or modified in transit.

**Remediation:** Add spec.tls entries (with a certificate Secret, e.g. issued by cert-manager) covering every host in spec.rules, and redirect HTTP to HTTPS in the ingress controller.

**Known limitations:** TLS terminated in front of the Ingress (e.g. at a cloud load balancer) is not visible and is reported.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Ingress: TLS](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/#tls)

## HX-NET-006

**Ingress injects NGINX configuration snippets** — high, networking

**Checks:** Detects Ingresses with ingress-nginx snippet annotations (configuration-snippet, server-snippet, auth-snippet, modsecurity-snippet, stream-snippet).

**Why it matters:** Snippets are inserted verbatim into the controller's NGINX configuration. Anyone who can create or edit an Ingress can use them to read the controller's service account token and every Secret it can access (CVE-2021-25742), or to proxy traffic anywhere.

**Remediation:** Replace snippets with dedicated annotations or controller configuration, and run the controller with allow-snippet-annotations: false.

**Known limitations:** Whether the controller actually honours snippets (allow-snippet-annotations) is controller configuration that Hardex does not read; the annotation is reported either way.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [CVE-2021-25742: ingress-nginx custom snippets](https://discuss.kubernetes.io/t/security-advisory-cve-2021-25742-ingress-nginx-custom-snippets-allows-retrieval-of-ingress-nginx-serviceaccount-token-and-secrets-across-all-namespaces/17860)

## HX-NET-007

**Retired ingress-nginx controller** — medium, supply-chain

**Checks:** Detects workloads running the community ingress-nginx controller image and IngressClasses served by it.

**Why it matters:** The Kubernetes project retired ingress-nginx: best-effort maintenance ended in March 2026 and no further releases or security fixes are published. An internet-facing component that will not receive security fixes accumulates exploitable vulnerabilities.

**Remediation:** Migrate to a maintained ingress or Gateway API implementation, and plan the migration for internet-facing clusters first.

**Known limitations:** Identified by image name (…/ingress-nginx/controller) and IngressClass controller (k8s.io/ingress-nginx); renamed mirrors of the image are not recognised.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Upgrading and application security practices](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Ingress NGINX retirement](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/11/11/ingress-nginx-retirement/)

## HX-NET-008

**Gateway listener without TLS** — medium, networking

**Checks:** Detects Gateway API listeners with protocol HTTP whose hostname is not also served by an HTTPS or TLS listener on the same Gateway.

**Why it matters:** Traffic to an HTTP-only listener crosses the network in clear text: credentials, session cookies and API tokens can be read or modified in transit.

**Remediation:** Add an HTTPS listener with certificateRefs for the hostname (for example issued by cert-manager), and keep the HTTP listener only to redirect to HTTPS with an HTTPRoute RequestRedirect filter.

**Known limitations:** An HTTP listener alongside an HTTPS listener for the same hostname is assumed to redirect; the HTTPRoutes are not inspected. TLS terminated in front of the Gateway (e.g. at a cloud load balancer) is not visible.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Gateway API: TLS configuration](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/guides/tls/)

## HX-NET-009

**Gateway accepts routes from every namespace** — medium, networking

**Checks:** Detects Gateway API listeners whose allowedRoutes.namespaces.from is All, or Selector with an empty selector.

**Why it matters:** Any namespace that can create an HTTPRoute can then attach it to the listener and claim its hostnames and paths: a tenant, or an attacker with a foothold in any namespace, can intercept traffic meant for another application, including credentials posted to it.

**Remediation:** Set allowedRoutes.namespaces.from to Same, or to Selector with a label selector matching only the namespaces that own the listener's hostnames. Pin hostnames on the listener so routes cannot widen them.

**Known limitations:** Selectors are not evaluated against namespace labels; only the empty selector is reported.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Network policies](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Gateway API: cross-namespace routing](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/guides/multiple-ns/)

## HX-NODE-001

**Kubelet allows anonymous requests** — high, nodes

**Checks:** Detects kubelet configurations that set authentication.anonymous.enabled to true.

**Why it matters:** The kubelet API can list pods, read logs and execute commands in containers. Anonymous access lets anyone who can reach port 10250 attempt those operations.

**Remediation:** Set authentication.anonymous.enabled: false and authentication.webhook.enabled: true.

**Known limitations:** Command-line flags that override the configuration file are applied only when the node is scanned with hardex scan --node; in manifests and other inputs they are not visible.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 4.2.1 Ensure that the --anonymous-auth argument is set to false](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Worker node segmentation](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-NODE-002

**Kubelet authorization disabled** — critical, nodes

**Checks:** Detects kubelet configurations with authorization.mode AlwaysAllow, or with webhook authentication explicitly disabled.

**Why it matters:** With AlwaysAllow, any client that authenticates to the kubelet (or any anonymous client, if anonymous auth is on) can execute commands in every container on the node.

**Remediation:** Set authorization.mode: Webhook and authentication.webhook.enabled: true.

**Known limitations:** Command-line flags that override the configuration file are applied only when the node is scanned with hardex scan --node; in manifests and other inputs they are not visible.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 4.2.2 Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Worker node segmentation](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-NODE-003

**Kubelet read-only port enabled** — medium, nodes

**Checks:** Detects kubelet configurations with a non-zero readOnlyPort.

**Why it matters:** The read-only port (historically 10255) serves pod specs and node information without any authentication or authorization, which aids reconnaissance and can leak environment variables.

**Remediation:** Set readOnlyPort: 0.

**Known limitations:** Command-line flags that override the configuration file are applied only when the node is scanned with hardex scan --node; in manifests and other inputs they are not visible.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 4.2.4 Verify that if defined, the --read-only-port argument is set to 0](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Worker node segmentation](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-NODE-004

**Kubelet does not protect kernel defaults** — low, nodes

**Checks:** Detects kubelet configurations that do not set protectKernelDefaults: true.

**Why it matters:** When enabled, the kubelet refuses to start if kernel tunables differ from its expected safe defaults, instead of silently modifying them.

**Remediation:** Set protectKernelDefaults: true after configuring the required sysctls on the node.

**Known limitations:** Command-line flags that override the configuration file are applied only when the node is scanned with hardex scan --node; in manifests and other inputs they are not visible.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Worker node segmentation](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-PATH-001

**Privilege-escalation path from workload** — critical, attack-paths

**Checks:** Searches for multi-step paths from each workload to cluster administrator (critical), to a cloud workload identity (high) or, failing those, to root on a node (high), combining container escape, token theft from pods that can share a node, workload creation, exec, token minting, RBAC escalation and cloud workload identities. Direct grants are reported by HX-RBAC-008 and HX-PATH-002, direct escapes by the HX-WL rules; this rule reports chains.

**Why it matters:** Real attacks chain weaknesses: an exploited web pod that can escape to its node can steal the token of a privileged controller scheduled on the same node. Each step alone may look acceptable; the chain is a full compromise — of the cluster, or of the cloud account behind it.

**Remediation:** Break the chain at its cheapest link, listed in the finding: remove the escape vector, keep powerful tokens off shared node pools (node selectors or dedicated pools), stop mounting tokens in pods that do not need them, narrow the RBAC grant or cloud role, or enforce Pod Security admission in the namespace.

**Known limitations:** Pods may share a node unless their nodeSelector or a single required node-affinity term makes their node sets provably disjoint; taints and preferred affinity are not modelled. Namespaces without a Namespace object in the input are assumed not to enforce Pod Security. Cloud identities are recognised from ServiceAccount annotations (EKS IRSA, GKE Workload Identity, Azure Workload Identity); EKS Pod Identity associations live outside Kubernetes and are not visible. Workloads in kube-system are not reported as starting points unless --include-system is set, but their tokens are considered.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Threat model](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [RBAC good practices: privilege escalation risks](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/rbac-good-practices/#privilege-escalation-risks)

## HX-PATH-002

**Workload token grants a cloud identity** — low, attack-paths

**Checks:** Reports workloads whose mounted service-account token is federated to a cloud identity through EKS IRSA (eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn), GKE Workload Identity (iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account) or Azure Workload Identity (azure.workload.identity/client-id plus the azure.workload.identity/use pod label).

**Why it matters:** Workload identity is the right way to give pods cloud access, but it extends the pod's blast radius into the cloud account. An inventory of which workloads hold which role is what reviewers need to keep those roles least-privilege; HX-PATH-001 reports chains through these identities from other workloads.

**Remediation:** Confirm the workload needs the identity, scope the cloud role to the resources it uses, and keep tokens off pods that do not need cloud access (a separate service account, or automountServiceAccountToken: false).

**Known limitations:** The cloud role's own permissions are not evaluated. EKS Pod Identity associations are configured in AWS, not Kubernetes, and are not visible.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Protecting sensitive cloud infrastructure](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Protecting Pod service account tokens](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-RBAC-001

**Wildcard RBAC permission** — high, rbac

**Checks:** Detects Roles and ClusterRoles that use "*" in verbs, resources or apiGroups. High for ClusterRoles, medium for Roles.

**Why it matters:** Wildcards grant every current and future permission in scope, including secrets, escalation verbs and resources introduced later by CRDs. They make least privilege impossible to verify.

**Remediation:** Replace wildcards with the explicit verbs, resources and API groups the subject needs.

**Known limitations:** Roles are reported whether or not they are bound; an unbound role is latent risk.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.3 Minimize wildcard use in Roles and ClusterRoles](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-RBAC-002

**cluster-admin granted** — high, rbac

**Checks:** Detects bindings to the cluster-admin ClusterRole. Bindings to service accounts or to broad groups are critical.

**Why it matters:** cluster-admin is unrestricted control of the cluster. A service account holding it turns any compromise of the pods using that account into full cluster compromise.

**Remediation:** Bind a purpose-built role with only the permissions required. Reserve cluster-admin for break-glass human access.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.1 Ensure that the cluster-admin role is only used where required](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-RBAC-003

**Read access to Secrets** — high, rbac

**Checks:** Detects roles that explicitly grant get, list or watch on Secrets without restricting resourceNames. High for ClusterRoles, medium for Roles.

**Why it matters:** Secrets hold credentials, including service account tokens in older clusters. list and watch return every secret's contents, so read access to secrets is effectively access to everything those credentials unlock.

**Remediation:** Remove the grant, or restrict it with resourceNames to the specific secrets required.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.2 Minimize access to secrets](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-RBAC-004

**RBAC privilege-escalation verb** — critical, rbac

**Checks:** Detects roles that grant escalate or bind on roles/clusterroles, or impersonate on users, groups or service accounts.

**Why it matters:** escalate and bind bypass RBAC's built-in escalation prevention, letting the holder grant themselves any permission. impersonate lets the holder act as any identity, including cluster administrators.

**Remediation:** Remove these verbs. If a controller genuinely needs them, isolate it with a dedicated service account and restrict resourceNames.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.8 Limit use of the Bind, Impersonate and Escalate permissions in the Kubernetes cluster](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [RBAC: privilege escalation prevention](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#privilege-escalation-prevention-and-bootstrapping)

## HX-RBAC-005

**Access to sensitive subresource** — high, rbac

**Checks:** Detects roles that grant pods/exec, pods/attach, pods/portforward, pods/ephemeralcontainers, serviceaccounts/token or nodes/proxy.

**Why it matters:** Exec and attach give a shell in other workloads (and their credentials). Ephemeral containers can inject a debug container into any pod. serviceaccounts/token mints tokens for other identities. nodes/proxy reaches the kubelet API directly, bypassing audit and admission.

**Remediation:** Remove the grant; provide debugging access through a separate, audited break-glass role.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.10 Minimize access to the proxy sub-resource of nodes](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.13 Minimize access to the service account token creation](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-RBAC-006

**Workload creation permission** — medium, rbac

**Checks:** Detects roles that grant create on pods or pod-creating controllers. Medium for ClusterRoles, low for Roles.

**Why it matters:** Anyone who can create a pod can run it as any service account in the namespace and mount any secret there, inheriting all of those permissions. Unless admission policy blocks it, they can also create privileged pods.

**Remediation:** Limit workload creation to deployment pipelines and controllers, and enforce Pod Security admission (restricted) in every namespace where it is granted.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.4 Minimize access to create pods](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [RBAC good practices: workload creation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/rbac-good-practices/)

## HX-RBAC-007

**Permissions granted to anonymous or all users** — high, rbac

**Checks:** Detects bindings whose subjects are system:anonymous or system:unauthenticated (critical), or system:authenticated / all service accounts (high).

**Why it matters:** These groups include every caller that can reach the API server. A grant to them is a grant to any attacker with network access or any compromised pod.

**Remediation:** Bind permissions to specific users, groups or service accounts.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Authentication](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-RBAC-008

**Workload holds dangerous API permissions** — high, rbac

**Checks:** Follows each workload's service account through RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings to the permissions its mounted token carries, and reports workloads that can read secrets, exec into pods, mint tokens, reach kubelets, create workloads (medium), escalate or impersonate, or control everything (critical).

**Why it matters:** Container compromise is common; what matters is what the stolen token can do next. A web server whose service account can read every secret turns one application bug into a cluster-wide breach.

**Remediation:** Give the workload a dedicated service account bound only to what it needs, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false if it never calls the API. Remove broad grants found through the listed binding.

**Known limitations:** Only bindings and roles present in the input are followed (plus the default cluster-admin, admin, edit and view ClusterRoles). Aggregated ClusterRoles, cloud IAM mappings and webhook authorizers are not evaluated. Workloads in kube-system are skipped unless --include-system is set.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.6 Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Authentication and authorization › Role-based access control](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Protecting Pod service account tokens](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [RBAC good practices](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/rbac-good-practices/)

## HX-SEC-001

**Secret values in manifest** — medium, secrets

**Checks:** Detects Secret manifests that carry their values inline (data or stringData).

**Why it matters:** Secret data is base64-encoded, not encrypted. A Secret manifest committed to version control exposes the credential to everyone with repository access, forever, including in history.

**Remediation:** Keep secret values out of manifests: use an external secret store (e.g. via the Secrets Store CSI driver or an external-secrets operator) or encrypt them at rest in the repository (e.g. SOPS, sealed secrets).

**Known limitations:** When scanning a live-cluster export, Secrets necessarily contain data; disable this rule for such scans.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.4.2 Consider external secret storage](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Secrets](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-SEC-002

**Credential in environment variable literal** — medium, secrets

**Checks:** Detects container environment variables whose name suggests a credential and whose value is written literally in the manifest instead of referencing a Secret.

**Why it matters:** Literal values live in the workload spec, which far more principals can read than Secrets (anyone with get on Deployments), and they are copied into version control and controller history.

**Remediation:** Move the value into a Secret and reference it with env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef, or mount it as a file.

**Known limitations:** Name-based heuristic: credentials under unremarkable names are missed, and non-secret values under credential-like names may be reported. Values are never included in findings.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.4.1 Prefer using Secrets as files over Secrets as environment variables](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Secrets](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-WL-001

**Privileged container** — critical, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers with securityContext.privileged set to true.

**Why it matters:** A privileged container has every capability and full access to host devices. Escaping to the node is trivial, and from the node an attacker can usually reach every other workload and the kubelet's credentials.

**Remediation:** Remove securityContext.privileged. If specific kernel access is needed, grant the single required capability instead and document why.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.2 Minimize the admission of privileged containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: Privileged Containers](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-002

**Host namespace sharing** — high, workloads

**Checks:** Detects pods that share the node's network, PID or IPC namespace.

**Why it matters:** hostNetwork exposes node-local services (including the kubelet and cloud metadata endpoints) and lets the pod sniff or spoof node traffic. hostPID allows inspecting and signalling every process on the node. hostIPC exposes shared memory of other workloads.

**Remediation:** Remove hostNetwork, hostPID and hostIPC. Expose services through a Service instead of the node network.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.3 Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host process ID namespace](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.4 Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host IPC namespace](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.5 Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host network namespace](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: Host Namespaces](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-003

**HostPath volume** — high, workloads

**Checks:** Detects pods that mount directories from the node's filesystem. Mounts of sensitive paths (root, /etc, container runtime sockets, kubelet state) are raised to critical.

**Why it matters:** HostPath mounts bypass container filesystem isolation. Writable mounts of sensitive paths allow node takeover; a mounted container runtime socket is equivalent to root on the node.

**Remediation:** Replace hostPath with emptyDir, a ConfigMap/Secret, or a PersistentVolumeClaim. If node access is unavoidable (e.g. a log collector), mount the narrowest path read-only and isolate the workload in a dedicated namespace.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.11 Minimize the admission of HostPath volumes](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: HostPath Volumes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-004

**Privilege escalation allowed** — medium, workloads

**Checks:** Detects Linux containers that do not set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false.

**Why it matters:** When allowed (the default), setuid binaries and file capabilities inside the image can raise a process's privileges, turning a low-privilege foothold into root inside the container.

**Remediation:** Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false on every container.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.6 Minimize the admission of containers with allowPrivilegeEscalation](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Restricted: Privilege Escalation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-005

**Container may run as root** — medium, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers that are not required to run as a non-root user (runAsNonRoot is not true at container or pod level), and containers explicitly configured to run as UID 0.

**Why it matters:** Root inside a container is root on the node's kernel interfaces. Combined with any container escape, misconfigured mount or kernel vulnerability, it maximises the attacker's starting privilege.

**Remediation:** Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true (pod or container level) and a non-zero runAsUser, and build images that run as a non-root USER.

**Known limitations:** If runAsNonRoot is unset, the effective user depends on the image's USER directive, which Hardex does not inspect.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.7 Minimize the admission of root containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › "Non-root" containers and "rootless" container engines](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Restricted: Running as Non-root](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)
- PSS: [Restricted: Running as Non-root user](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-006

**Dangerous Linux capability added** — high, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers that add Linux capabilities outside the Pod Security Standards Baseline allow-list. Capabilities that commonly enable escape (SYS_ADMIN, SYS_MODULE, SYS_PTRACE, BPF, ALL, ...) are critical.

**Why it matters:** Capabilities split root's power into pieces; several of those pieces are each sufficient to escape the container or tamper with the node.

**Remediation:** Remove the capability from securityContext.capabilities.add. Prefer drop: [ALL] and add back only NET_BIND_SERVICE if a low port is required.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.8 Minimize the admission of containers with the NET_RAW capability](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.9 Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: Capabilities](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-007

**Capabilities not reduced to minimum** — low, workloads

**Checks:** Detects Linux containers that do not drop ALL capabilities, or that add any capability other than NET_BIND_SERVICE.

**Why it matters:** Container runtimes grant a default capability set that most applications never use. Dropping them removes kernel attack surface at no cost to the workload.

**Remediation:** Set securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] and, only if needed, add: ["NET_BIND_SERVICE"].

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.9 Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Restricted: Capabilities](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-008

**Seccomp profile not enforced** — medium, workloads

**Checks:** Detects Linux containers whose effective seccomp profile is not RuntimeDefault or Localhost. An explicit Unconfined profile is raised to high.

**Why it matters:** Seccomp filters the system calls a container may make. Without it, the full kernel syscall surface is reachable, and many container-escape exploits rely on syscalls that the runtime default profile blocks.

**Remediation:** Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault at pod level (or Localhost with a reviewed profile).

**Known limitations:** Clusters with the kubelet's seccompDefault feature enabled apply RuntimeDefault implicitly; Hardex cannot observe that from manifests and reports the unset profile.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.6.2 Ensure that the seccomp profile is set to docker/default in your Pod definitions](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Hardening container environments](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: Seccomp](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)
- PSS: [Restricted: Seccomp](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-009

**Writable root filesystem** — low, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers that do not set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem to true.

**Why it matters:** A writable root filesystem lets an attacker who gains code execution drop tools, modify binaries and persist changes for the life of the container.

**Remediation:** Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount an emptyDir for any path the application must write (e.g. /tmp).

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.6.3 Apply SecurityContext to your Pods and Containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Immutable container file systems](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-WL-010

**Missing resource limits** — low, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers without a memory limit (low) or CPU limit (info), unless a LimitRange in the same namespace supplies a default.

**Why it matters:** Unbounded containers let one compromised or faulty workload exhaust node resources and deny service to its neighbours, including node-critical agents.

**Remediation:** Set resources.limits.memory on every container (and resources.requests.cpu, plus a CPU limit where your scheduling policy calls for one), or define a namespace LimitRange with defaults.

**Known limitations:** CPU limits are reported at info severity because they can cause throttling; many operators deliberately rely on CPU requests only.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Network separation and hardening › Resource policies](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-WL-011

**Mutable image tag** — medium, supply-chain

**Checks:** Detects containers whose image has no tag or uses the latest tag, and is not pinned by digest.

**Why it matters:** An untagged or latest image can change between deployments without any manifest change, so what runs is neither reviewed nor reproducible, and a compromised registry push is picked up silently.

**Remediation:** Reference images by an immutable version tag and, preferably, a digest (image@sha256:...).

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Building secure container images](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- Kubernetes: [Images: image names](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/)

## HX-WL-012

**Image not pinned by digest** — info, supply-chain

**Checks:** Detects versioned image references that are not pinned by digest.

**Why it matters:** Version tags can be overwritten in most registries. Only a digest guarantees that the reviewed image is the one that runs.

**Remediation:** Pin the image by digest (e.g. registry/app:1.4.2@sha256:...), ideally maintained by an automated dependency updater.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Building secure container images](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-WL-013

**Service account token auto-mounted** — low, workloads

**Checks:** Detects pods that mount a Kubernetes API token without opting out, neither in the pod spec nor on a ServiceAccount found in the input.

**Why it matters:** Most applications never call the Kubernetes API, yet every compromised container with a mounted token can. The token's RBAC permissions become the attacker's.

**Remediation:** Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod spec or its ServiceAccount; enable it only for workloads that call the API, with a dedicated least-privilege ServiceAccount.

**Known limitations:** If the ServiceAccount is not part of the scanned input, its automount setting cannot be checked and the pod is reported.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.1.6 Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Protecting Pod service account tokens](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)

## HX-WL-014

**Host port bound** — medium, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers that bind a port directly on the node with hostPort.

**Why it matters:** hostPort exposes the container on the node's address, bypassing Service-level controls and NetworkPolicy assumptions, and pins the workload to nodes where the port is free.

**Remediation:** Remove hostPort and expose the workload through a Service (ClusterIP, or an Ingress/LoadBalancer with restricted sources).

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.12 Minimize the admission of containers which use HostPorts](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: Host Ports](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-015

**AppArmor disabled** — high, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers whose AppArmor profile is explicitly set to Unconfined, through the securityContext field or the legacy annotation.

**Why it matters:** AppArmor confines file, mount and capability use even for root. Disabling it removes a layer that blocks several known escape techniques.

**Remediation:** Remove the Unconfined setting so the runtime default applies, or set securityContext.appArmorProfile.type: RuntimeDefault.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.6.3 Apply SecurityContext to your Pods and Containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Hardening container environments](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: AppArmor](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-016

**Custom SELinux context** — high, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers that set an SELinux type outside the container types allowed by the Pod Security Standards, or that set a custom SELinux user or role.

**Why it matters:** Changing the SELinux context can place a container in a domain with host-level access (e.g. spc_t or unconfined_t), defeating mandatory access control.

**Remediation:** Remove seLinuxOptions.user and .role, and use one of container_t, container_init_t, container_kvm_t or container_engine_t (or leave type unset).

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.6.3 Apply SecurityContext to your Pods and Containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Hardening container environments](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: SELinux](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-017

**Unmasked /proc mount** — high, workloads

**Checks:** Detects containers with securityContext.procMount set to Unmasked.

**Why it matters:** The default /proc mount masks paths that leak host information or allow kernel tuning. Unmasking them exposes the host to the container.

**Remediation:** Remove procMount or set it to Default.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.6.3 Apply SecurityContext to your Pods and Containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: /proc Mount Type](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-018

**Unsafe sysctl** — medium, workloads

**Checks:** Detects pods that set sysctls outside the Pod Security Standards safe set.

**Why it matters:** Unsafe sysctls are not namespaced or not isolated between pods; setting them can affect the node and every other workload on it.

**Remediation:** Remove the sysctl, or run the workload on dedicated nodes where the kubelet explicitly allows it.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.6.3 Apply SecurityContext to your Pods and Containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: Sysctls](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-019

**Non-standard volume type** — low, workloads

**Checks:** Detects pods using volume types outside the Pod Security Standards Restricted allow-list (hostPath is reported separately by HX-WL-003).

**Why it matters:** In-tree network and node volume types bypass PersistentVolume access controls and are a common source of unexpected data or credential exposure.

**Remediation:** Use a PersistentVolumeClaim (backed by a CSI driver) instead of an in-tree volume source.

**References:**

- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Restricted: Volume Types](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)

## HX-WL-020

**Windows HostProcess container** — critical, workloads

**Checks:** Detects Windows containers that run as HostProcess, at pod or container level.

**Why it matters:** A HostProcess container runs directly on the Windows node with host-level access; it is the Windows equivalent of a privileged container.

**Remediation:** Remove securityContext.windowsOptions.hostProcess.

**References:**

- CIS: [CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v2.0 5.2.10 Minimize the admission of Windows HostProcess containers](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/kubernetes)
- NSA-CISA: [NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance v1.2 (August 2022) — Kubernetes Pod security › Pod security enforcement](https://media.defense.gov/2022/Aug/29/2003066362/1/1/0/CTR_KUBERNETES_HARDENING_GUIDANCE_1.2_20220829.PDF)
- PSS: [Baseline: HostProcess](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)
